# [1.1.0](https://github.com/prod-forge/frontend/compare/v1.0.0...v1.1.0) (2026-11-09)

### Bug Fixes

* **a11y:** put the visible text into the names of Prev and the status toggle ([0c3e88a](https://github.com/prod-forge/frontend/commit/0c3e88a959d4342aa32388b43a7caea0f2154978))
* **ci:** sync assets under the assets/ prefix that CloudFront reads ([6173931](https://github.com/prod-forge/frontend/commit/617393128cfd6b585808ae41c7175dfbb2636ce9))
* make the Claude deny hooks actually deny ([8925e32](https://github.com/prod-forge/frontend/commit/8925e32a57817eda81d4610396654a5cde69f160))
* **mobile-client:** install the @sentry/react-native version Expo SDK 58 expects ([69bf7b1](https://github.com/prod-forge/frontend/commit/69bf7b140146d72c1d395eefb0694221838432b9))
* **mobile-client:** keep sendDefaultPii explicit under the Sentry 8.28 types ([c8806c4](https://github.com/prod-forge/frontend/commit/c8806c4144c55050ce3afda62f34d13a7e15fba4))
* paste over-limit descriptions in ui-web tests instead of typing them ([89fce8b](https://github.com/prod-forge/frontend/commit/89fce8b4de446856d903e1dd83552a3f9dc41519))
* **ui-web:** drop aria-pressed from the status toggle whose name changes ([d3dc9a0](https://github.com/prod-forge/frontend/commit/d3dc9a071467701fccf7ea65251f54d97109ca29))
* **ui-web:** remove the forgot password form from the login form ([d5e89a8](https://github.com/prod-forge/frontend/commit/d5e89a89a91f1ad633a6f8fc64e5ba472d0671fc))
* **ui-web:** trap focus in the modal and return it to the opener ([26be9e8](https://github.com/prod-forge/frontend/commit/26be9e8563a2f67b83a67dd14394932a3a66180a))
* **web-client:** mask all text in Sentry Replay ([9b97cdf](https://github.com/prod-forge/frontend/commit/9b97cdff64ec3c46419d452684fb4574ce5d371a))

### Features

* **web-client:** show a not found page for unknown paths ([404256c](https://github.com/prod-forge/frontend/commit/404256c9adf4dd7cfb71705902c0f896d8a09dbc))

detail.readme: _AI made writing the code easy. Running it in production is still hard._ This repository holds the web and mobile clients in one NX monorepo, with a shared design system. It answers: how do I build, ship, and keep web and mobile clients healthy? Part of Prod Forge — start with the organization overview: https://github.com/prod-forge ## Stack | Layer | Tools | | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | | Web Client | React · Vite · Redux Toolkit · Tailwind CSS · NX | | Mobile Client | Expo · React Native · Redux Toolkit | | Quality | ESLint · Prettier · Husky · Commitlint · CI/CD | The full stack table is on the organization page: https://github.com/prod-forge ## Getting started Requires Node 24 and the backend API running (see the [backend guide](https://github.com/prod-forge/backend#readme)). ```shell npm ci cp .env.example .env # VITE_API_BASE_URL is required for a build (absolute URL ending with "/"); dev falls back to the /api/v1/ proxy npm run dev # web client cp apps/mobile-client/.env.example apps/mobile-client/.env # EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL, mobile client only npm run dev:mobile # mobile client (Expo) ``` # Table of contents - [1. Mobile Client](guide/mobile-client.md) - [Why Expo](guide/mobile-client.md#why-expo) - [What Is Shared and What Is Not](guide/mobile-client.md#what-is-shared-and-what-is-not) - [Project Layout](guide/mobile-client.md#project-layout) - [Metro in a Monorepo](guide/mobile-client.md#metro-in-a-monorepo) - [Platform Adapters](guide/mobile-client.md#platform-adapters) - [Theming From Tokens](guide/mobile-client.md#theming-from-tokens) - [Testing](guide/mobile-client.md#testing) - [Not Covered](guide/mobile-client.md#not-covered) # Conclusion A frontend is easy to start and hard to keep healthy. The first screen takes an afternoon. What takes years is everything around it: two clients that must agree on the same rules, a bundle that grows a little with every feature, an error a user saw that nobody can reproduce, a release that has to be rolled back on a Friday evening, and a design that drifts a pixel at a time until nobody trusts it. This repository is an attempt to show that work, not just the screens. The stack - React, Expo, Redux Toolkit, Tailwind, NX - is not the point. These are just tools. The principles behind them apply to almost any client, whatever framework comes next. What matters is the thinking: - Why does sharing a store and an API layer between web and mobile pay off only with a strict dependency direction? - Why should a design system live in the repository, with tokens, stories and visual tests, and not in a design file? - Why does a client need its own observability when the backend already logs every request? - Why is the browser an untrusted environment, and what does that change about tokens and configuration? These are not advanced topics. They are basic requirements for any client that real users depend on. The goal of Prod Forge is to make these practices visible, understandable, and reusable. ## What comes next Open work is tracked in the [roadmap](roadmap.md) and summarized on the [organization page](https://github.com/prod-forge). ## A final thought The best time to set up these practices is at the beginning of a project. The second best time is now. A client without error tracking leaves you guessing about what users actually saw. A design system without visual tests drifts until nobody trusts it. A bundle without a budget only grows. A release without a rollback path turns a small mistake into an outage. None of these things are difficult to set up. They are just easy to skip. This project exists as a reminder not to skip them. # Intentionally out of scope - Passwords, refresh tokens, sign-up and an identity provider: the clients sign in with the backend's login stub, see [Security](guide/security.md#authentication) - Store release of the mobile app: no EAS Build, EAS Submit or over-the-air updates, see [Mobile Client](guide/mobile-client.md#not-covered) - Running CI: the workflows exist but are disabled on purpose, see the [roadmap](roadmap.md) # Contributing We welcome any kind of contribution, please read the guidelines: [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md) # The MIT License [LICENSE](LICENSE)
